questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol was consumed

questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly it was consumed, and body weight. How often someone drinks does not affect their current BAC.

questions.question: When following a car, which part of the lane is best for riding?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver ahead can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: Why should you not change gears on railroad tracks?

options.text: Other drivers may not be expecting you to change gears.
The uneven surface may make it more difficult to switch gears.

questions.explanation: Do not shift gears while crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle could stall while on the tracks.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Cover the clutch and the brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
questions.explanation: Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time. This is helpful when riding through areas with potential hazards.

questions.question: What are the two most common types of motorcycle helmets?
questions.explanation: The two main helmet types are three-quarter and full-face. A full-face helmet provides the best protection.

questions.question: When stopped, which gear should you stay in?
questions.explanation: Downshift through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before each ride. Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week for safe riding.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol is consumed
How often the drinker consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: How do motorcycle headlights compare to car headlights?

options.text: Usually more powerful than a car's headlights.
Usually just as powerful as a car's headlights.
Usually not as powerful as a car's headlights.
Usually larger than a car's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually not as powerful as a car's headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What helps you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and use both brakes. Avoid sudden movements. Stay away from the center of the lane and follow tire tracks from cars. Watch for hazards like oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: Studies show that most riders in crashes:

options.text: Don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
Brake the front tire too much and don't brake the rear tire enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
questions.explanation: Most riders in crashes don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.

questions.question: A child passenger should:

options.text: Sit in front of the operator.
Not be able to reach the footrests.

questions.explanation: A child should always sit right behind the operator. If a child sits in front, they may not balance well and could get in the way of the controls.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle or sidecar, don't ride too far right because:

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar sits on the right side. If you ride too far right, the sidecar can go off the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the right rear wheel can leave the road if you get too close to the right edge.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have curved, or convex, mirrors. These mirrors:

options.text: Are easy to get used to right away.
Make cars seem closer than they actually are.
Provide a narrow view of the road.
Make cars seem farther away than they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars seem farther away than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. They make objects look farther away than they really are. Practice judging distances in convex mirrors if you're not used to them.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, ride in a:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation works best for two-wheeled motorcycles. Three-wheeled motorcycles are too wide for this. Ride in a single-file line.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips under five miles long at speeds slower than 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center of your lane.
Stay in the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or from the front, stay in the center of your lane. Riding closer to the passing vehicle is dangerous.

questions.question: Which formation is best for a group entering a curve?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for groups to stay close while keeping space between riders. Use a single-file line for curves, turns, and entering or exiting highways.

questions.question: What happens when you brake while turning a curve?

options.text: It is the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more traction as you lean into the curve.
You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When your motorcycle leans into a turn, your tires use some of their grip to turn. This means less grip is available for braking.

questions.question: How should you choose your lane position?

options.text: Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.
Always ride in the right part of the lane.
Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose where you will be most visible to other drivers and where you can keep space around you. Different situations call for different positions.

questions.question: Why should you not move to the far side of your lane when being passed?

options.text: It stops the other driver from moving back too early.
It encourages the other driver to move back into your lane too early.
It makes the other driver pass you faster.
It encourages more drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages the other driver to move back into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: If you move to the far side of your lane, the passing driver may think it is safe to return to your lane before it really is. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed to stay safe.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which instruction should you NOT give?

options.text: Board the motorcycle only after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Feel free to talk whenever you want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel free to talk whenever you want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should avoid talking or moving around. This keeps you focused on riding. Passengers should board after the engine starts, sit forward without crowding you, and hold on firmly.

questions.question: What collects in the center of a traffic lane?

options.text: The safest place for motorcycles to ride.
The spot where drivers see motorcycles best.

questions.explanation: The center of the lane is where debris and oil drippings from vehicles collect. Utility hole covers and other hazards are also found in the center of lanes.
